pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Bodsham Church of England
Primary School
Bodsham Church of England Primary School is a small rural school in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Our setting helps children learn to appreciate the natural environment and to develop a profound respect for all of creation.
We have spaces in some year groups. So, if you are looking for a school place right now, or are interested in starting school in our Ofsted Strong Early Years Provision in 2027, please get in touch to arrange a visit to our friendly little school!
I am proud to be Headteacher of a school I love and have been part of for many years. Having worked here for so long, I know our children, families and community well, and I truly value the strong sense of collaboration between staff, pupils, parents and the wider community. I am passionate about helping every child reach their full potential and believe that children flourish best when we work together in partnership.
Our Christian values of love, creativity and strength sit at the heart of all that we do, shaping our learning, our relationships, and the way we care for one another and the world. My hope is that every child feels nurtured, encouraged and inspired to speak out, so that they grow into confident, compassionate individuals who flourish and go on to make a positive difference in the world.
Building on our Christian values, we nurture the qualities and skills that help every child flourish both in school and beyond. Through our Curriculum Aims, children develop independence, communication skills, self-expression, resilience, creativity, self-belief, curiosity through enquiry, and an appreciation of our diverse world. We are passionate about creating a warm and nurturing environment where every child feels happy, valued and inspired to achieve their very best.
I look forward to welcoming you!
Mrs Mary StephenHead Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - Starting School
pageCache.text:
Starting School
ARE YOU LOOKING FOR A SCHOOL PLACE?
Thank you for considering Bodsham Church of England Primary School for your child. You are making an important decision and we wish to do all we can to support you in this process.We currently have spaces in some year groups, including our current Reception Class so please get in touch if you'd like to come and look around!
We offer personal tours of the school with our headteacher. We feel this will allow families to see our amazing school in action in a friendly and personal way.
Please contact the school office to book a tour at a time that suits you, or to let us know you would like to attend one of our open days.
You can apply for a Reception place at our school via the KCC website www.kent.gov.uk/ola between November 2025 and mid-January 2026
For all other applications, please contact the school office.
Please refer to the admissions section of our website for full details.
When a school place has been accepted, we use the summer term to offer a programme of transition events to support a smooth and enjoyable start to school life. These include nursery visits, home visits, stay and play sessions, and a teddy bear's picnic with Barley the Bodsham Bear.
We look forward to welcoming you and your child to our community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - School Clubs
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
Breakfast Club - Monday to Friday
Mrs Wenham runs Breakfast Club from 8am five days a week. Bagels, crumpets, toast and waffles are on offer for the children until around 8.20am. The cost of Breakfast Club per child is £3.50 per day, regardless of whether your child has breakfast or not. Bookings can be made via Arbor.
We offer after school clubs and activities for children Monday - Friday each week
Children can join our new wraparound care provider, TeachSport Canterbury. The club runs until 6pm and costs £12 per child. Snacks will be provided.
After School Sessions with Teachsport can be booked here.
Children can join in with free lunchtime activities clubs as part of our extended curriculum. These include nature club, library club, doodle club, and various sports activities throughout the week. No need to sign up, just come and join the fun..

Woodpeckers
See what the Woodpeckers got up to in 2023-24!
GLOBAL RECYCLING DAY – 18TH MARCH 2025
To celebrate Global Recycling day, we would like to remind you that we are representatives for Terracycle. We can recycle some objects that you can’t put in your household recycling bins.
Simply bring these items to Bodsham School and place them in the boxes outside our classroom. We will send the items off to be recycled. Your waste can be turned into new items, such as outdoor furniture, and soft play coverings. This will prevent these items from ending up in landfill, or worse, our rivers and oceans.
Help us to be a better friend to our community, as we try to be God’s caretakers on Earth.
The Woodpeckers Class
Any Pringles cans
Any cheese packaging
All bread wrappers
Visit to the Roman Museum
As part of their History topic, the Woodpeckers had a great day at the Canterbury Roman Museum!
Fort Burgoyne Trip in May
The Woodpeckers had a great day out at Fort Burgoyne, Dover. They took part in bug hunts and practised their classifying skills! In the afternoon, the children collaborated in trust games, culminating in a treasure hunt. The weather was perfect and we all enjoyed taking our learning outside of the classroom!

As part of the Canterbury Festival, Bodsham hosted a poetry and music festival for our Year 5 and 6 children Last week. Organised jointly with Langdon Primary School, the children were treated to some spooky artefacts to inspire their writing, and were wowed by singing from an expert Opera singer who taught them some songs and helped them understand how their voices work. Thank you Ms Allen from Bodsham and Mrs Newton from Langdon for organising such an inspiring event!

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - Homework
pageCache.text:
HOMEWORK
Reading Challenge
The most important homework you can do is to read every day. Older children should be encouraged to read independently, but it remains important that they read every day.
Literacy Homework
Children in KS1 & 2 are provided with a work book to structure their homework. Exercises for the children to complete at home will include punctuation, spelling and grammar that become increasingly challenging each year.
Spellings
The children in years 2-6 also bring home spellings each week. Children in Year 1 are encouraged to learn 'tricky words' that do not easily fit into a phonetic approach to spelling. Spellings are revised each week.
You can assist by helping your child find an effective way of learning his/her spellings. Give them as much encouragement as possible. Look say cover write check.
Times Tables
Children are expected to have memorised all times tables up to 12x12 by the end of Year 4. They will be given specific tables to learn each year to build up this instant recall, starting in Year 1 with 2x, 5x and 10x. Constant practice at home will really help children achieve this aim and Y2- Y5 will have weekly tables tests.
Don't forget to mix up the order of the tables, and to ask questions in different ways, such as "how many sevens are there in 42?"
Mathematics Homework
Children in Y1-Y6 will be given a mathematics workbook. Teachers will ask children to complete specific pages each week that link to the topic being studied in class at that time.
Homework in the Early Years
In reception, along with daily reading, teachers will suggest a Family Learning Task that parents and children can complete together in the Family Learning Book. These tasks are optional, but can be lot of fun!
Give your child lots of praise!

pageCache.text:
School Council
The School Council is comprised of two representatives from each year group from years one to six and meets regularly to discuss a variety of topics and issues that affect the school such as equipment, clubs, fundraising events and curriculum issues.
Each school council representative collects the views of those in their class and shares those views at the meetings; ensuring that the views of all children in the school are shared. School Council representatives feedback the minutes from the meetings to their class.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to help all our children develop into confident, responsible young people who are ready to take the next steps in their lives.
We teach the National Curriculum In the context of our Christian values of Love, Creativity and Strength. We have identified eight key attributes we seek to develop in our children through our curriculum. These are known as our ‘curriculum aims’
We have created a curriculum map for each year group which explains how what is taught seeks to develop each of these attributes. Our children receive a broad and rich programme of learning experiences based on the Early Years Foundation Stage in Year R and the National Curriculum in Key Stage 1 and 2.
For more information about our curriculum please contact Mrs Stephen.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodsham Church of England Primary School - History of Bodsham School
pageCache.text:
History of Bodsham School
Henry John Nancollas MBE, head of Bodsham C of E primary school from 1954 to 1986, died earlier this year from COVID-19. Born in Llanelli, South Wales in 1927, his enthusiasm for rugby, cycling and dogs developed at an early age. His happiest memories from his youth included playing rugby for Llanelli grammar school at Stradey Park and acquiring a Russian Borzoi called Boris.
After training as a teacher at Trinity College, Carmarthen he completed his military service from 1946 to 1948 and joined Hurst Primary School in Bexley. He quickly came to the attention of Freda Weal, another young teacher at the school. A tandem bicycle was bought, and they married in 1950.
After a few years teaching in Canterbury, aged 26 John was appointed as the head of Bodsham School and ‘Sir and Mrs Sir’ moved to School House. Here he got to grips with the challenges of running a rural school with ancient plumbing, a school kitchen in the old vicarage stables, and a home without electricity. Bodsham School became his life’s work, here he could invest in the development of young minds, in glorious surroundings, without the constraints that a larger school might bring.
Although appointed an Inspector of Schools in the 1960s, he chose to spend the rest of his career at Bodsham. Many former students will recall his creative approach to learning, not least through major projects such as Bodsham New Town and the Round the World Yacht race. He was frequently asked to lecture at conferences about his work.
Outside school John was an enthusiastic member of the Evington Players, clerk to the Parish Council, and was involved in the building of Evington Hall. However, his main passion was the school and the young people he taught. Right to the end of his life he talked about his wonderful boys and girls and what they meant to him.
On his retirement from Bodsham, John was awarded an MBE for services to education though he maintained that it was for services to rural plumbing. He and Freda moved to Kennington, where one of his greatest joys was past students calling in. He continued to ride his bicycle into his late 80s. The deaths of Freda in 2015 and his son Tim in 2018 hit him hard and his memories of Bodsham became even more important. He is survived by his daughter Sarah and granddaughter Bryony.
John Nancollas, a proud Welshman who gave his life to Bodsham School will be remembered fondly by the hundreds of children he inspired.
